title: Field Sensor Playbook for Emergent Model Disruptions
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Objective: Build a compact, repeatable playbook and lightweight detection pipeline ("field sensors") that surfaces early signals of emergent model disruptions (new entrants, API drift, regional availability shocks, quantization regressions) and ties them to runnable fallback actions and procurement triggers.

Scope:
- Define top 8 high-signal indicators that predict meaningful customer impact within 72 hours (examples below).
- Implement a minimum-viable ingestion path that synthesizes telemetry from: hosted API latency/error metrics, SDK client telemetry (agent pings), regional model availability feeds, and weekly sample evals run against a small probe prompt set.
- Produce a compact mapping from detected signal -> recommended action: (e.g., pin to fallback model variant; enable increased caching; engage procurement; raise SE alert).
- Provide starter dashboards and automated Slack alerts for on-call and GTM.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- Detection precision >= 60% for disruptions that lead to customer-facing degradation (validated against 6-week historical incidents).
- Mean time from detection to recommended action surfaced <= 10 minutes.
- 3 documented operator runs (runbook drills) demonstrating automatic fallback flow end-to-end.

Proposed high-signal indicators (prioritized):
1) Regional latency spike co-occurring with model-specific 5xx rate increase (weight: high).
2) Persistent token-generation slowdown at sequence lengths representative of top customer workloads (weight: high).
3) Divergence between canonical eval set answers and live model outputs (alert when semantic similarity < 0.75 over 100 probes).
4) Sudden increase in fallback invocation attempts from SDKs (client-side telemetry).
5) Model variant availability toggles (provider-side) for >2 regions in a short window.
6) Unexpected quantization-induced hallucination patterns detected by lightweight heuristics on sampled outputs.
7) Unusual cost-per-token volatility for a model flavor (economics signal).
8) Social/PR signals: public provider status pages indicating incidents (synthesized via webhooks).

Detection heuristics and trade-offs:
- Combine signal sources using a small rule engine (weighted scoring) rather than full ML initially to keep interpretability and fast iteration.
- Thresholds will be adaptive: start conservative to limit false positives, then loosen after 2 weeks of controlled ops drills.
- Trade-offs: higher sensitivity increases noise for SRE/SE teams; to mitigate, surface confidence and suggested remediation (automated vs. manual).

Ingestion & infra outline (MVP):
- Ingest metrics: existing telemetry streams (Cloudwatch/Prometheus), SDK pings (batched), and provider availability hooks.
- Lightweight probe runner: schedule 100 short prompts across model variants/regions every 15 minutes; store compact hashes + embeddings for drift detection.
- Rule engine: serverless function (fast iteration) that emits alerts to Slack and writes incidents to linear via webhook.
- Dashboard: Grafana/Console tile showing top signals and active recommendations.

Runbook & actions mapping (example flows):
- Latency+5xx in region X for model M -> 1) increase cache TTL for common prefixes; 2) autopromote fallback variant M-compact for region X for 30 minutes; 3) notify SE on duty and attach diagnostic links.
- Eval divergence detected for semantic-critical prompt set -> 1) flag model for immediate canary rollback; 2) pause new deployments on that model family; 3) open procurement ticket if degradation persists >24h.

Dependencies and open questions:
- Dependency: lightweight client telemetry SDK change to add 1x/min heartbeat (ENG-PR required).
- Dependency: telemetry retention for probe outputs needs 14 days (cost implication).
- Open Q: acceptable false positive rate for GTM/CS alerts before we need suppression logic?
- Open Q: who signs off on automated autopromote actions for enterprise accounts (default off for high-tier customers).

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: noisy signals cause alert fatigue -> mitigation: phased rollout with opt-in pilot customers and suppression thresholds.
- Risk: probe runner costs grow -> mitigation: limit probes per model family and use hashed/sample-based storage.

Next milestones (two-week cadence):
1) Week 0-1: finalize signal definitions, confirm SDK heartbeat path, draft PRD (confluence link).
2) Week 2-3: engineering spike: probe runner prototype + rule engine prototype, internal demo.
3) Week 4: pilot with 3 internal customers, runbook drills, adjust thresholds.
4) Week 6: wider pilot including selected production tenants and enable automatic fallback for non-enterprise tenants.
